author: william e winkler
html:
Entity resolution (record linkage) has been a major area of research since the 1950s. There was a big expansion after
Rahm, E., and Do, H.-H. (2000), “Data Cleaning: Problems and Current Approaches,” IEEE Bulletin on Data Engineering, 23 (4), 3-13.

This is my sixth keynote at a workshop at a major international cs conference.

https://sites.google.com/site/dinaworkshop2015/invited-speakers

I introduced the generalized software in two short courses that I taught at the University of London and again lectured on the ideas when I was back in Cambridge at the Isaac Newton Institute (talks organized by Peter Christen).

The following paper gives a few more details and references.

https://www.census.gov/srd/papers/pdf/RRS2018-05.pdf

Our record linkage systems are ML that must do unsupervised learning in ~500 regions into which the U.S. is divided. In 1990, we had to match the entire U.S. in less than six weeks as part of a large system to meet deadlines established in U.S. law.
